bullets.title: S&P 500 hits ATH on earnings/Iran deal optimism; Nasdaq +3.3%, chips rally 4-day best since 2020
bullets.body: S&P 500 and Dow hit record closes (first since June) as strong Q2 earnings (47%+ YoY blended EPS growth, 78% beat rate) combined with Strait of Hormuz diplomacy. Brent crude fell 5%+ to ~$79 and WTI ~$75.77 as Iran signaled willingness to negotiate; NDX recovered ~935bps in 4 sessions. 75% of S&P by weight eligible to restart buybacks by end of next week, and Nasdaq short interest remains elevated providing squeeze fuel.

bullets.title: Fed's Schmid hawkish: policy 'not restrictive,' AI investment itself is inflationary
bullets.body: KC Fed President Schmid (non-voter) said current monetary policy is not restrictive, tighter policy is needed to reach 2% inflation target, and AI investment is driving inflation the Fed should not ignore. He is the fifth Fed official since last week's FOMC to signal openness to further tightening; market pricing ~57-58% probability of a September rate hike.

bullets.title: Iran/Hormuz deal optimism deflates oil 5%; geopolitical window still fluid
bullets.body: Markets rallied sharply on Qatar-brokered interim Hormuz proposal backed by Oman, but Iran denied knowledge of U.S.-side talks and the Houthis claimed a ballistic missile strike on a Saudi oil tanker in the Red Sea. Polymarket pricing only ~32% probability of normalized Hormuz traffic by September 30, and API crude stocks rose an unexpected 2.7M barrels. Trump said 'moving along very nicely' and expects clarity in 48 hours.

bullets.title: JPMorgan: Mag7 trades 2 std devs below mean valuation; AI capex ROI is durable/visible
bullets.body: JPM argues Mag7 implies ~30% upside to 1 std dev below mean and ~56% to return to average valuation. AMZN servers break even in <3 years, MSFT estimates ~30% ROIC on AI capex, GOOGL backlog growing faster than capex. Only META remains a 'show-me story' with no deals or revenue products launched. CSP backlog grew >150% YoY to ~$1.7T vs capex growth ~80%.

bullets.title: SpaceX exclusively commits to NVIDIA; plans 2GW compute by year-end, 10GW by end 2027
bullets.body: SpaceX Q2 revenue $7.8B (+92% YoY, beat $6.82B est), adj. EBITDA $3.5B (+191% YoY), AI revenue $2.56B (+213% QoQ) from $14.1B in new cloud bookings. Musk confirmed SpaceX will build exclusively on NVIDIA going forward, expects 'significant percentage' of NVIDIA GPUs in 2027. Wolfe calculates SpaceX's ~6GW incremental 2027 compute at ~$35B/GW = ~$200B NVDA revenue from this single customer, exceeding Street's $160B incremental datacenter growth estimate. SPCX shares fell 7-11% on $18.4B capex and 911.5M share lockup expiring Aug 6.

bullets.title: AMD -9% on elevated expectations despite data center beat; Helios ramp the bull case
bullets.body: AMD Q2 revenue $11.54B (+50% YoY) and EPS $1.66 beat consensus, Q3 guided to $13.0B vs Street $12.5B. Data center +107% YoY to $6.72B; management projects data center revenue to more than double in CY27 and server CPU to grow >70% YoY. Stock fell ~9% on capex surprise ($808M vs $299M expected) and positioning overhang; warrants seen as multi-year dilution risk. Most analysts maintain Buy; avg PT raised to $590, but some await MI4xx/Helios volume confirmation.

bullets.title: ANET +10%: raises FY26 growth guide to 40%, supply constraints easing
bullets.body: Arista Q2 revenue $3.04B (+38% YoY, +7.4% vs consensus), operating margin 49.9% (+340bps above); raised full-year guidance to 40% YoY growth from 28% prior on supply chain improvements. AI fabric target remains ≥$3.5B, Campus ≥$1.25B. Morgan Stanley, Citi, and JPM all raised PTs to $215-$250 range. Supply tightness expected to persist industry-wide through at least 2028.

bullets.title: AI infrastructure power constraint: US faces ~38GW shortfall through 2028; no nationwide moratorium likely
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley estimates ~38GW US power shortfall through 2028 as biggest AI buildout constraint, with 300+ local moratoria since 2023. Geopolitical competition with China makes nationwide bans unlikely; hyperscalers shifting toward behind-the-meter generation. Data center capex expected to remain elevated through at least next year.

bullets.title: US drafts ban on Chinese optical transceivers; COHR, LITE, AAOI key beneficiaries
bullets.body: Trump administration drafting restrictions on US imports of Chinese data-center optical transceivers; tech sector +4%+ on the news. COHR already received up to $50M CHIPS Act funding to quadruple InP wafer capacity in Texas. Jefferies sees low materialization risk but notes supply chain vulnerability: missing one batch of transceivers can idle billion-dollar GPU clusters. Sell-side consensus names COHR and AAOI as primary beneficiaries; FN and LITE as secondary.

bullets.title: SHOP +23%: Q2 revenue $3.58B (+34% YoY), Q3 guided low-30s% vs Street ~27%
bullets.body: Shopify crushed Q2 with GMV +31.5%, revenue $3.58B vs consensus $3.45B, FCF $654M vs $541M; Q3 guide of low-30s% revenue growth and mid-to-high-20s% gross profit far above consensus. Cloud/AI infrastructure costs accelerated (+$37M YoY in COGS vs +$22M in Q1), a potential headwind. UBS maintains Neutral noting GP deceleration risk; JPM and others bullish on the durable growth trajectory.

bullets.title: BKNG +9.7%: travel demand resilient; Q3 guidance below on Middle East/flight headwinds
bullets.body: Booking Q2 room nights +5% YoY (beat +2-4% guide), revenue $7.35B vs $7.18B est, adj. EBITDA $2.65B beat; but Q3 guided room nights +3-5% (below Street) as Middle East conflict reduces long-haul airline capacity. Management raised cost-savings target to $650M. Domestic/intra-regional travel resilient while long-haul pressured. Citi, Mizuho, MS raised PTs to $230-$240 range. LLMs account for <1% of room nights.

bullets.title: Equity dispersion at record highs; correlations at historical lows — JPM sees tactical squeeze fuel
bullets.body: JPMorgan equity volatility strategy notes dispersion reached record highs in Aug 2026 earnings season with correlations at historic lows across index-stock and sector-stock layers. US hedge fund gross exposure de-grossing in July was most negative except 2020/2022; post de-grossing, gross flows expected to rebound into mid-September. Retail investors sold $847M in single stocks (3.2nd percentile) while preferring ETFs ($1.065B bought).

bullets.title: Korea memory selloff overdone per Morgan Stanley and GS; HBM pricing +100% YoY in 2027
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley upgrades Korea to Overweight after ~40% drawdown driven by leveraged ETF unwinds (~70% decline in Samsung/SK Hynix leveraged AUM from $40B peak). GS and JPM both reiterate Buy on SK Hynix; HBM pricing expected to increase ~100% YoY in 2027 on tight supply and AI demand. SK Hynix and Samsung are also evaluating Chinese AMEC etching equipment for China fabs as US export control hedge.

bullets.title: Euro area Q3 growth revised up; Germany/France industrial data weak but services better
bullets.body: JPMorgan raised Eurozone Q3 GDP forecast 0.25ppt to 1.25% annualized on firm July composite PMI (+2pts to ~51.7 services, 52.9 manufacturing output). Spain raised +1ppt to 3%. France industrial production fell -1.1% MoM and -1.7% YoY in June; Germany and France composite PMIs remain near 50 (Germany 49.8, France 49.4). JPM's Q3 forecast is well above ECB's 0.5% expectation.

bullets.title: BOJ minutes hawkish; US-Japan yen intervention confirmed at $50-100B range
bullets.body: BOJ June minutes showed members expect consumer inflation to rise significantly in H2 and flagged upside risks to 2% target. Treasury Secretary Bessent confirmed US joined Japan's yen intervention ('for stability of Asia') in a $50-100B range via EUR/JPY; he expressed confidence in BOJ Governor Ueda and attributed Japan's inflation to weak yen and elevated energy prices. Japan margin trading at highest since 1990.

bullets.title: Atlanta Fed GDPNow spikes to nearly 6%; S&P earnings revisions 5th straight quarter positive
bullets.body: Atlanta Fed GDPNow jumped to nearly 6% Q3 growth. S&P 500 blended 2Q EPS growth tracking ~47% YoY; 78% beat rate (above 76% 1y avg); 8 of 11 sectors seeing >10% EPS growth. NTM EPS estimates up 15bps for 5th straight quarter. Info tech trades at 20x, one-year valuation low vs. 23x 10-year average.

bullets.title: SpaceX Starlink mobile to compete directly with VZ/T/TMUS by end of 2027
bullets.body: SpaceX plans to acquire customers from AT&T, Verizon, and T-Mobile via next-gen Starlink Mobile V2 satellites in 2027, using EchoStar spectrum and femtocells on Starlink dishes rather than large base stations. VZ fell 2.7%, T fell 1.9%, TMUS fell 1.3% pre-market on the comments. JPM also raising SpaceX PT to $240 from $225.

bullets.title: $8.3T in money market funds at record; retail bought ETFs not stocks into the July low
bullets.body: Money market funds hit $8.3T all-time high, signaling elevated defensive positioning and potential dry powder. JPM data shows retail investors sold $847M in single stocks (3.2nd percentile) during the July decline while preferring ETFs. Hedge fund gross exposure to Korea fell from 3.8% peak to 2.7%; US L/S net leverage decline typically followed by rebounds.

bullets.title: DIS beats Q3 EPS by 12%; raises buyback to $9B; parks at high end of HSD guidance
bullets.body: Disney Q3 adj. EPS $2.06 (+28% YoY) beat consensus $1.84-1.86; parks OI +27% YoY, SVOD margins 12.9% vs 6.6% prior year. FY26 12% EPS growth reaffirmed; Experiences guided to high end of high-single-digit range. Disney selling 50% stake in A+E for proceeds to fund $9B share repurchases (up from $8B). Q4 headwinds: Moana below expectations and softer SVOD advertising.

bullets.title: ALAB beats with massive Sept Q guide of $540-560M vs $412M Street; Trainium 3 driving CY27 to ~$3B
bullets.body: Astera Labs Q2 revenue $392M (+27% QoQ) beat consensus; Sept Q guide of ~$550M midpoint was 33% above Street. Trainium 3 content estimated at $600-1,000/XPU with 2.8M units in CY27 implying ~$1.7-2.0B of CY27 revenue. Scorpio becomes largest product family in Sept Q ahead of schedule. UBS raises PT to $425 (Neutral); Morgan Stanley raises PT to $382; JPM raises PT to $465. Risk: AWS Trainium 4 with NVLink Fusion could benefit MRVL.
